Use case: style-transfer. Production UV base-colour atlas for a rebuilt realistic AH-64-inspired attack helicopter in Rule Of War.
Image 1 is the exact EDIT TARGET: newly unwrapped geometry's flat material-colour atlas. Preserve every UV island silhouette, position, scale, orientation and all gutters exactly. Green islands are painted aircraft metal, dark islands are graphite / rubber / black fittings, grey islands are metal, blue islands are glass. Do not repack.
Image 2 is the prior game texture STYLE REFERENCE only: retain its subdued olive palette and realistic aircraft wear, but reduce widespread scraped-through paint. Image 3 is a real Apache MATERIAL REFERENCE only: subdued olive painted panels, realistic hardware and actual aircraft surface character. Do not draw the assembled aircraft or copy the photo into the sheet.
Paint credible, restrained, high-quality military aircraft detail within the exact existing UV shapes: crisp fine panel lines, fasteners, access panel outlines, rubber seals, faint service stencils with no large text, larger localized maintenance scuffs, fine scratches, slight edge paint chips, dusty creases and limited exhaust grime. Most paint remains intact deep dusty olive / drab, with subtle faded panel variation. No tank camouflage and no evenly scattered noisy speckling. Keep long thin dark blade islands near-black graphite, with subtle leading-edge abrasion; do not paint camouflage or broad pale scratches on rotor blades. Rubber remains matte charcoal. Bare fittings show dark steel.
Base colour only under neutral diffuse unlit illumination: no long cast shadows or bright baked highlights, no perspective, no assembled vehicle view. Preserve UV borders precisely and keep the background gaps black. Square texture, crisp fine detail.
